title: Counit-normalized source comparison for coordinate diagonals
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $n\geq1$ and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $Y$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme, let $h:U\to Y$ be smooth separated of finite type and pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, and let $e:U\to A=\mathbf A^d_Y$ be an etale $Y$-map, where $U$ is finite type over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. Put $p:A\to Y$, so $h=pe$. Use fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] $W=U\times_YU$, $W_A=A\times_YA$, with first projections $p_U,p_A$ and diagonal closed immersions $\Delta_U,\Delta_A$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $Z=U\times_AU\subset W$ and $O=W\setminus(Z\setminus\Delta_U(U))$, with its induced open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. Write $i:O\hookrightarrow W$ and $q=(e\times e)|_O:O\to W_A$. Use the constructible exceptional inverse images [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], derived pullbacks [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and $\omega_g=Rg^!\Lambda_{\operatorname{target}(g)}$. For any smooth separated finite-type $g$ with closed section $s$, put $C(g,s)=Ls^*\omega_g$ [def-pur-section-invariant]. Let $\alpha_h:C(p_U,\Delta_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_h$ and $\alpha_p:C(p_A,\Delta_A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_p$ be the specified diagonal base-change maps [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]. Here $p_U$ denotes the projection from $W$ when used in $C(p_U,\Delta_U)$. All maps $h,p,e$ and the smooth projections are compactifiable [thm-nagata-compactification]. Composition of exceptional adjoints, followed by the canonical etale identification $Re^!=Le^*$, gives
$$c_e:\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*\omega_p.$$
This is the finite constructible transport of the canonical ordinary-etale adjoint-locality comparison of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], using the trivial etale dualizing object of [lem-pur-co-smooth-etale-locality] and the tensor/composition comparisons of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness]. Apply the same etale exceptional comparison first to the open $i$ and then to $q$, and pull back along the section $\Delta_U:U\to O$, using $q\Delta_U=\Delta_Ae$. The resulting section-invariant comparison is an isomorphism
$$a:C(p_U,\Delta_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*C(p_A,\Delta_A).$$
For the counit-mate base-change normalization [def-pur-co-smoothness], these actual morphisms satisfy
$$(Le^*\alpha_p)\circ a=c_e\circ\alpha_h.$$
The comparison uses the two projections, with $p_{r,A}q=e\,p_{r,U}|_O$ for $r=1,2$ and $pe=h$, and is unchanged by further open restriction near the diagonal. It is an equality of specified adjunction comparisons, rather than existence of an isomorphism of their objects.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-chart-cartesian-domain] with $X=U$, $f=h$, $j=1_U$ and $V=Y$. It gives exactly the stated $O$, the Cartesian square of centres and the separated finite-type domains. Put $V_0=U\times_Y A$, $r:V_0\to U$, $v:V_0\to A$, $b=(e,1):V_0\to W_A$, and $t=(p_{1,U},e p_{2,U}):W\to V_0$. The square $(t,p_{2,U};v,e)$ is Cartesian: on test schemes its points are precisely pairs $(u_1,u_2)$ with $h(u_1)=h(u_2)$. Thus $t$ is a base change of $e$, while $(b,r;p_A,e)$ is Cartesian. The etale base-change assertion [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] makes $t,b$ etale. The separated finite-type base-change lemma [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] applies to these maps and to $r$. [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] gives smoothness of $r$ by base change from $p$ and of $er$ by composition with the dimension-zero smooth map $e$. Finite type over the field makes the schemes Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; the field is Noetherian since its ideals are $0$ and $1$. Nagata [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies all required compactifications. In particular none of the compact-support comparisons below is applied outside its Noetherian compactifiable domain.

proof.text: First calculate with ordinary etale origins, writing $\Omega_f=f^\times\Lambda$, $B_{f,g}:g'^*\Omega_f\to\Omega_{f'}$ for the inverse-exchange/counit transpose, and $E_{u,f}:\Omega_{fu}\to u^*\Omega_f$ for the inverse of adjoint locality. [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] supplies the latter natural isomorphism, with the composite-adjunction normalization. [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] makes every $B$ used below invertible: its vertical morphism is $h$, $p$ or a smooth projection. Here $\Lambda$ is finite, annihilated by $\ell^n$, and $\ell$ is invertible on every scheme. [lem-pur-finite-site-counit-projection-transport] carries the actual counits, conjugate compositors and exchange transposes to the specified pro-etale maps and reflects equality on bounded constructible inputs. These inputs are the smooth dualizing objects, their pullbacks and section invariants, hence bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude by [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness, def-pur-section-invariant]. Thus the ordinary calculation proves an equality of the required maps after transport; it does not assume an unbounded pro-etale exceptional adjunction.

source.place: Step 3, first paragraph: composing adjunctions and the two diagonal source maps; inherited proof Step 5

proof.text:
Use the proper-support/sum normalization [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] for the datum in [lem-amb-etale-left-comparison-base-change]. Instantiate the latter with its $u=e$, $f=p$, change of base $h:U\to Y$, $f'=r$, $u'=t$, and its two upper pullbacks $v,p_{2,U}$. The three required squares are the square defining $V_0$, its pullback along $e$, and the self-product square for $h$. Taking its right-adjoint mates, using [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] for pasting and changing the adjunctions, gives
$$E_{t,r}\,B_{h,h}=t^*B_{p,h}\,p_{2,U}^*E_{e,p}.$$
Both sides go from $p_{2,U}^*\Omega_h$ to $t^*\Omega_r$. Specifically $B_{h,h}$ is the transpose of $h^*\varepsilon_h\operatorname{Ex}_{h,h}^{-1}$ and $B_{p,h}$ of $h^*\varepsilon_p\operatorname{Ex}_{p,h}^{-1}$; the two locality maps are the conjugates of the etale left comparisons. The cited left-comparison equation identifies the inverse-exchange factors, and mate-pasting identifies their composite counits. This proves the displayed equation for these specified transposes, rather than by choosing isomorphisms between their endpoints.

proof.text:
The base change of $p$ along $h=pe$ is obtained by first changing base along $p:A\to Y$ and then along $e:U\to A$. Compatibility with composite changes of base in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], transposed by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], gives
$$B_{p,h}=B_{p_A,e}\,b^*B_{p,p}.$$
Use the pullback-composition constraints of [lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal]. Put $m=bt=e\times e$ and
$$T=t^*B_{p_A,e}^{-1}\,E_{t,r}:\Omega_{p_U}\longrightarrow m^*\Omega_{p_A}.$$
Substituting the preceding equation in Step 3 and cancelling the invertible $t^*B_{p_A,e}$ gives
$$T\,B_{h,h}=m^*B_{p,p}\,p_{2,U}^*E_{e,p}.$$
Each $B$ is invertible by Step 2. This identity already lives on the whole self-product $W$; no assertion that $m$ makes the square of diagonals Cartesian has been used.

proof.text:
Transport to finite constructible categories as in Step 2. For a smooth $j$ followed by the etale $e$ put $D_j=Rj^!(\eta_e)c_{e,j}:\omega_{ej}\to\omega_j$, with $\eta_e:\omega_e\to\Lambda$ the fixed unit. [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization](3) says $B_{p_A,e}=D_r E_{b,p_A}^{-1}$. Associativity of the conjugate compositors [thm-sf-comp-composition, lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] and naturality at $\eta_e$ give
$$E_{t,r}D_{p_U}=t^*D_r\,E_{t,er},\qquad t^*E_{b,p_A}\,E_{t,er}=E_{m,p_A}.$$
Therefore $T D_{p_U}=E_{m,p_A}$, by substituting $B_{p_A,e}^{-1}=E_{b,p_A}D_r^{-1}$ into the definition of $T$. This describes the comparison for $m$ by exactly its etale exceptional compositor and target unit.

Put $u=p_Ui$ and let $s:U\to O$ be the diagonal. The same composition equations, including [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization](2), give
$$i^*T=E_{q,p_A}D_u^{-1}E_{i,p_U}^{-1}.$$
This is the specified comparison: invert open locality to pass from $i^*\omega_{p_U}$ to $\omega_u$, invert the target-etale unit map $D_u$, then use etale locality for $q$. Pull back by $s$ and use $qs=\Delta_Ae$; hence $a=L\Delta_U^*T$. Every factor is invertible. For a further open $i':O'\hookrightarrow O$ containing the section, the identical equation with $ii'$ follows from the same associative compositors and identity normalization. Pullback by its section cancels the open factors, so $a$ is unchanged. The invertibility of $D_j$ is also part of the normalized target-etale comparison in (3).

proof.text:
By [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], with its specified normalization [def-pur-co-smoothness], $\alpha_h=L\Delta_U^*B_{h,h}^{-1}$ and $\alpha_p=L\Delta_A^*B_{p,p}^{-1}$, inserting the section identities. Pull back the last equation of Step 4 along $\Delta_U$. Since $p_{2,U}\Delta_U=1_U$ and $m\Delta_U=\Delta_Ae$, it becomes
$$a\,\alpha_h^{-1}=Le^*(\alpha_p^{-1})\,c_e,$$
where $c_e$ is the transported $E_{e,p}$ from Step 2. Pullback coherence [lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal] and its transported comparisons identify the two occurrences of each constraint. Multiply on the left by $Le^*\alpha_p$ and on the right by $\alpha_h$. This is exactly $(Le^*\alpha_p)a=c_e\alpha_h$. The construction used both projection equations and $pe=h$, and Step 5 proves the required invariance under further restriction. No orientation enters.
